title: Maharashtra projects revenue deficit despite strong tax base, low debt: Rpt
description:
Maharashtra has a relatively strong tax base and one of the country's lowest debt burdens, but has budgeted for a revenue deficit of 0.7 per cent of its Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) in 2026-27, a report has said.
The report by PRS Legislative Research notes that the state's own tax revenue, including state Goods and Services Tax (GST), stamp duty and VAT, is estimated at 7.7 per cent of its GSDP, higher than the average of seven per cent.
Maharashtra's outstanding debt is below 20 per cent of its GSDP, in line with the recommendation of the FRBM Review Committee (2017). It is among only three states meeting this benchmark, the other two being Gujarat and Odisha.
The state's fiscal deficit is budgeted at 2.6 per cent, also below the 16th Finance Commission's recommendation.
The outstanding liabilities at the end of March 2026 are Rs 9 lakh crore and the GSDP is Rs 49.3 lakh crore as per 2025-26 budget estimate.
